title: [Livestream 23/11/2024] Changes in annual spending by a particular UK school in 1981, 1991 and 2001
prompt: The three pie charts below show the changes in annual spending by a particular UK school in 1981, 1991 and 2001. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie chart gives information about how a school in the UK allocated its budget to five categories in three different years, 1981, 1991, and 2001.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, it is clear salaries made up the biggest proportion of each yearly budget, and teachers received the largest share collectively, while insurance was the least significant cost overall.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the major components, teachers’ salaries accounted for 40% of the annual expenditure in 1981, half of the budget in 1991, and finally, 5% less than that figure in the final year, at 45% in 2001. This is three times higher than the amount going to the remaining staff at the school in 2001, which experienced a relative decline throughout the period, as the figure was initially up to 28% in 1981. Oddly, furniture and equipment spending stood at 15% in the first year, dipped by two-thirds to 5% by the next recorded period, before it regaining its position again, ultimately ending up at 23% in 2001.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: The portion of annual spending used for school resources, such as books, came in at 15% in 1981, but declined to only 9% in the next 20 years. This is in stark contrast to the insurance spending trend, which was gradually allocated more funding, rising fourfold from a negligible 2% to 8% in the final year.
